title: Pekudei: Moses blessed them (Exodus 39:43)
hook: Moses sees the finished work and blesses the workers

segments.voice: Yesterday, the refrain of the last chapters: as the Lord commanded Moses. Your line was as it was asked. Today, the work is done.

The end of a big job has its own kind of quiet. A house renovated, a wedding pulled off, a school play performed, a garden finally planted. The people who did the work stand back, tired, a little proud, waiting. And very often, nobody says anything. In the desert, the craftspeople bring every finished piece of the sanctuary to Moses: the tent, the ark, the curtains, the clothes. He looks it all over. And then he does the thing so many finished jobs never get.
screen: `THE END OF A BIG JOB.` → `OFTEN, NOBODY SAYS ANYTHING.` → `MOSES LOOKS IT ALL OVER.`

segments.voice: In the JPS 1917 translation: "And Moses saw all the work, and, behold, they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, even so had they done it. And Moses blessed them." Three steps. He sees. He recognizes that they did it right. And he blesses them. The rhythm has been heard before. At the end of the sixth day of creation, Genesis says: "And God saw every thing that He had made, and, behold, it was very good." Readers have noticed the echo, and more: the work is finished, the sanctuary completed, a blessing given, all language that recalls the creation of the world. Some readers hear the building of the sanctuary told as a small creation, with Moses looking at it the way God looked at the world. What did he say? The verse doesn't tell us. Rashi offers an answer from the midrash: Moses said, may it be God's will that the divine presence rest on the work of your hands. And Rashi connects it to Psalm ninety, which the Book of Psalms itself calls a prayer of Moses, and which ends by asking God to establish the work of our hands. So the first thing Moses does with the finished sanctuary isn't to use it, or to correct it, or to move on. It's to turn to the people who made it and bless them, and their hands.
screen: `HE SAW, AND BEHOLD.` · `AN ECHO OF CREATION.` · `MAY THE PRESENCE REST ON YOUR WORK.` · `ESTABLISH THE WORK OF OUR HANDS.` · then, large: `BLESS THE WORKERS.`

segments.voice: Think of something someone around you finished recently, a meal, a repair, a hard semester, and picture it the way Moses looked over every piece. Notice what they did well, specifically, and the sentence that would show them you really saw it and wish good things for the work of their hands.
Pekudei. The portion where the work is finished, and Moses sees it, and blesses the people who made it.
Your line: bless the workers. First he saw the work, then he blessed. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: When the sanctuary was finished, what did Moses actually do first?
options: He looked it over, saw it was done as commanded, and blessed the people who made it.
He checked every piece for mistakes and sent the flawed ones back to be remade.
He gave the craftspeople the leftover gold as their pay for the work.
chat.meaning: Moses saw they had done it as the LORD commanded, and blessed them; Rashi says he prayed God's presence would rest on their work.
